thread:
jordan: quick heads-up — ran a ropecurve pass across Mistral/Mixtral/Qwen kernels on the long-ctx bench. saw a KV-cache growth mismatch on the Mixtral head-kv path that lines up with a perplexity drift after ~28k tokens. attaching rough traces and a couple profiling snippets.

maya: can you paste the trace? was this NTK or linear variant?

jordan: NTK variant mostly, but we ran YARN and linear as control. NTK shows the divergence earliest.

kai: interesting — is the leak in allocation count or stale pointers? any allocator logs?

jordan: allocator counts looked stable. it's more like stale KV pointers being reused incorrectly in the Mixtral kernel switch branch. see excerpt:

```
# perf snapshot (abridged)
model: mixtral-8x8
rope_variant: ntk
seq_len: 32768
step: 278
kv_entries: 8.1M -> 8.9M  # unexpected growth per 1k steps
latency_p95: 198ms -> 215ms
perplexity: 12.1 -> 18.6 (spike)
stack: runtime.kernel_headkv_swap -> runtime.kv_commit_if_needed -> runtime.cache_mark_reuse
```

olga: oof. does the kernel selection heuristic flip to a different kernel at the same token boundary? maybe a bundling fallback that doesn't clear temp buffers.

jordan: yes — kernel auto-switching kicks in around that token length for mixtral when batch-sizing heuristics change (continuous batching + shard fallback). suspect stale buffer when switching from fio-optimized kernel to head-kv-unified kernel.

maya: can we reproduce with a deterministic small harness? maybe run single-chat with synthetic tokens to 35k and `--trace-kv`?

jordan: I ran a deterministic harness: `./bench_longctx --model mixtral-8x8 --rope ntk --seq 35000 --batch 1 --trace-kv` — reproduction is stable. attaching the small snippet of trace lines: 

```
TRACE: kv_alloc id=0x7f9f2 size=2048
TRACE: kv_commit id=0x7f9f2 used=1024
TRACE: kv_reuse id=0x7f9f2 tag=HEAD_KV
TRACE: kernel_switch from=fio_opt to=headkv_unified
TRACE: kv_reuse id=0x7f9f2 tag=HEAD_KV  # later, but stale length
ERROR: perplexity_regression at step=279
```

kai: thanks. two quick action items: 1) add a GC pass on kernel_switch to forcibly clear tmp buffers, 2) tighten kernel selection boundary to avoid switching mid-session for certain ropecurve shapes. both are cheap to try.

olga: agree. also add an assert in head-kv read path to validate expected kv-length vs tag. will catch earlier.

perf-bot: CI-run queued: perf/longctx/mixtral-ntk-repro (job 4821).

maya: on the heuristics side, our batching config currently uses `batch_heuristic: adaptive-boundary` which allows multi-kernel swaps when average seq crosses thresholds. propose `batch_heuristic: session-sticky` for long-lived sessions (>16k) to pin kernel choice.

jordan: patch draft:

```
// runtime/config.h
enum BatchHeuristic { ADAPTIVE_BOUNDARY, SESSION_STICKY };
// default fallback for longctx
if (session.seq_so_far > 16000) cfg.batch_heuristic = SESSION_STICKY;
```

kai: sounds reasonable. but be careful: session-sticky can worsen latency for mixed workloads. add telemetry flag: `sticky_longctx_enabled` to A/B.

jordan: added telemetry + feature flag in the local branch. will run abtest on dev cluster. perf-bot job will show p95 and tok-cost.

olga: for safe ranges per-model: early notes — Mistral-7B: NTK safe to 48k with session-sticky; Mixtral-8x8: safe to 32k if head_kv_dim <= 128 and sticky enabled; Qwen-7B: linear variant seems safest beyond 64k. we should put these into the model-profiles DB once validated.

maya: can we also add a small diagnostic that emits `rope_scale_profile` at kernel-switch points so we can correlate the rotational phase vs kv reuse? small perf cost but valuable.

jordan: good idea. implemented lightweight sampling to log `rope_alpha` and `kv_length` at switches. adding to the reproduce run and CI.

perf-bot: perf/longctx/mixtral-ntk-repro (job 4821) finished: p95 regression +7% baseline -> investigating artifacts.

kai: next steps: (1) run CI with GC-on-switch patch (2) run session-sticky AB (3) add assert in head-kv path + diagnostic logs (4) compile model-profiles draft. I'll take (1) and (3). Jordan take (2) and (4)?

jordan: yep, I'll run the AB on dev and open PR with model-profiles draft. tagging @maya for instrumentation review.

maya: on it. thanks all :+1:

olga: filing a short incident note in postmortems/ if CI finds a regression in canary.

jordan: will follow up with the PR link once ready.
